vocabulary.definition: in a way that is difficult or impossible to imagine
vocabulary.example: The size of the black hole was unimaginably small, even compared to an atom.

vocabulary.definition: the theoretical radiation emitted by black holes due to quantum effects near the event horizon
vocabulary.example: The black hole would decay through Hawking radiation, converting its mass into energy.

vocabulary.definition: a unit of energy equal to one trillion joules
vocabulary.example: The black hole's mass would be converted into 450 terajoules of energy.

vocabulary.definition: the gravitational forces that cause deformations on a celestial body due to the gravitational pull of another object
vocabulary.example: The tidal forces from the black hole would rip apart individual cells due to their strength.

vocabulary.definition: having the shape of an ellipse; elongated and curved
vocabulary.example: The Moon's orbit would become highly elliptical due to the presence of the black hole.
The black hole's presence perturbed the orbits of the planets in the Solar system.
